source_text: Sed enim ordo rationis et fidei auctoritas digestis uocibus et litteris domini admonet nos post haec credere etiam in spiritum sanctum, olim ecclesiae repromissum, sed statutis temporum opportunitatibus redditum. est enim per Ioelem prophetam repromissus, sed per Christum redditus. in nouissimis, inquit, diebus effundam de spiritu meo super seruos et ancillas meas. dominus autem: accipite spiritum sanctum; quorum remiseritis peccata, erunt remissa; et quorum retinueritis, erunt retenta. hunc autem spiritum sanctum dominus Christus modo paracletum appellat, modo spiritum ueritatis esse pronuntiat. qui non est in euangelio nouus, sed nec noue datus. nam hic ipse et in prophetis populum accusauit, et in apostolis aduocationem gentibus praestitit. nam illi ut accusarentur merebantur, quia contempserant legem: et qui ex gentibus credunt, ut patrocinio spiritus adiuuentur merentur, quia ad euangelicam peruenire gestiunt legem. differentia sane in illo genera officiorum, quoniam in temporibus differens ratio causarum: nec ex hoc tamen ipse diuersus, qui haec sic gerit, nec alter est, dum sic agit, sed unus atque ipse est, diuidens officia sua per tempora et rerum occasiones atque momenta. denique apostolus Paulus: habentes, inquit, eundem spiritum, sicut scriptum est: credidi, propter quod locutus sum, et nos credimus, ideo loquimur. vnus ergo et idem spiritus, qui in prophetis et apostolis; nisi quoniam ibi ad momentum, hic semper. ceterum ibi, non ut semper in illis inesset, hic, ut in illis semper maneret: et ibi mediocriter distributus, hic totus effusus; ibi parce datus, hic large commodatus; nec tamen ante resurrectionem’ domini exhibitus, sed per resurrectionem Christi contributus. rogabo enim aiebat, patrem, et alium aduocatum dabit uobis, ut uobiscum sit in aeternum, spiritum ueritatis. et: cum uenerit aduocatus ile, quem ego missurus sum uobis a patre meo, spiritum ueritatis, qui de patre meo procedit. et: si non abiero ego, aduocatus ille non ueniet ad uos: si autem ego abiero, remittam illum ad uos. et: cum uenerit spiritus ueritatis, ille uos diriget in omnem ueritatem. et quoniam dominus in caelos esset abiturus, paracletum discipulis necessario dabat, ne illos quodammodo pupillos, quod minime decebat, relinqueret, et sine aduocato et quodam tutore desereret. Hic est enim qui ipsorum animos mentesque firmauit, qui -euangelica sacramenta distinxit, qui in ipsis illuminator rerum diuinarum fuit, quo confirmati pro nomine domini nec carceres nec uincula timuerunt; quin immo ipsas saeculi potestates et tormenta calcauerunt, armati iam scilicet per ipsum atque firmati, habentes in se dona, quae hic idem spiritus ecclesiae Christi sponsae quasi quaedam ornamenta distribuit et dirigit. hic est enim qui prophetas in ecclesia constituit, magistros erudit, linguas dirigit, uirtutes et sanitates facit, opera mirabilia gerit, discretiones spirituum porrigit, gubernationes contribuit, consilia suggerit, quaeque alia sunt charismatum dona componit et digerit; et ideo ecclesiam domini undique et in omnibus perfectam et consummatam facit. Hic est qui in modum columbae, posteaquam dominus baptizatus est, super eum uenit et mansit, habitans in solo Christo plenus et totus, nec in aliqua mensura aut portione mutilatus, sed cum tota sua redundantia cumulate distributus et missus, ut ex illo delibationem quandam gratiarum ceteri consequi possint, totius sancti spiritus in Christo fonte remanente, ut ex illo donorum atque operum uenae ducerentur, spiritu sancto in Christo affluenter habitante. hoc etenim iam prophetans Esaias aiebat: et requiescit, inquit, super eum spiritus sapientiae et intellectus, spiritus consili et uirtutis, spiritus scientiae et pietatis, et implebit eum spiritus timoris dei, hoc idem atque ipsum et alio in loco ex persona ipsius domini: spiritus domini super me; propter quod unxit me, euangelizare pauperibus misit me. similiter Dauid: propterea unxit te, deus, deus tuus oleo laetitiae a consortibus tuis. de hoc apostolus Paulus: guz enim spiritum Christi non habet, hic non est eius; et: vbi spiritus domini, tht libertas. Hic est qui operatur ex aquis secundam natiuitatem, semen quoddam diuini generis, et consecrator caelestis natiuitatis, pignus promissae hereditatis, et quasi chirographum quoddam aeternae salutis; qui nos dei faciat templum, et nos eius efficiat domum. qui interpellat diuinas aures pro nobis gemitibus ineloquacibus, aduocationis implens officia, et defensionis exhibens munera, inhabitator corporibus nostris datus, et sanctitatis effector; qui id agens in nobis ad aeternitatem et ad resurrectionem immortalitatis corpora nostra producat, dum illa in se assuefacit cum caelesti uirtute misceri, et cum spiritus sancti diuina aeternitate sociari. erudiuntur enim in illo et per ipsum corpora nostra ad immortalitatem proficere, dum ad decreta ipsius discunt se moderanter temperare. hic est enim "qui contra carnem desiderat, quia caro contra ipsum repugnat. hic est qui inexplebiles cupiditates coercet, immoderatas libidines frangit, illicitos ardores exstinguit, flagrantes impetus uincit, ebrietates reicit, auaritias repellit, luxuriosas comissationes fugat, caritates nectit, affectiones constringit, sectas repellit, regulam ueritatis expedit, haereticos reuincit, improbos foras exspuit, euangelia custodit. De hoc idem apostolus: on enim spiritum mundi accepimus, sed spiritum qui ex deo est. de hoc exsultat, et dicit: puto autem quia et ego spiritum dei habeo. de hoc dicit: et spiritus prophetarum prophetis subiectus est. de hoc refert: spiritus autem manifeste dicit, quia in nouissimis temporibus recedent quidam a fide, attendentes spiritibus seductoribus, doctrinis daemoniorum, in hypocrisi mendacia loguentium, cautertatam in hoc spiritu positus nemo umquam dicit anathema Iesum: nemo negauit Christum dei filium, aut repudiauit creatorem deum: nemo contra scripturas ulla sua uerba depromit: nemo alia et sacrilega decreta constituit: nemo diuersa iura conscribit. in hunc quisquis blasphemauerit, remissionem non habet, non tantum in isto saeculo, uerum etiam nec in futuro. hic in apostolis Christo testimonium reddit, in martyribus constantem fidem religionis ostendit, in uirginibus admirabilem continentiam signatae castitatis includit, in ceteris incorrupta et incontaminata doctrinae dominicae iura custodit, haereticos destruit, peruersos corrigit, infideles arguit, simulatores ostendit, improbos quoque corrigit, ecclesiam incorruptam et inuiolatam perpetuae uirginitatis et ueritatis sanctitate custodit.
pass_a_gloss: For the order of reason and the authority of faith, having arranged the words and letters of the Lord, admonish us to believe also in the Holy Spirit, who was promised to the church and given at the appointed times. For He was promised through the prophet Joel, but given through Christ. In the last days, He says, I will pour out my Spirit upon my servants and handmaids. The Lord says: Receive the Holy Spirit; whose sins you forgive, they will be forgiven, and whose sins you retain, they will be retained. The Lord Christ calls this Holy Spirit a paraclete and declares Him to be the Spirit of truth. He is not new in the Gospel, nor was He given newly. For this same Spirit accused the people in the prophets and provided advocacy to the nations in the apostles. For they deserved to be accused because they despised the law, and those who believe from the nations deserve to be helped by the advocacy of the Spirit because they strive to attain the law of the Gospel. There is indeed a difference in the kinds of offices, since the reason for the causes differs at different times. Nevertheless, He who does these things is not different, nor is He another when He acts in this way, but He is one and the same, dividing His offices through times and occasions and moments. Finally, the apostle Paul says: Having the same Spirit, as it is written, I believed, therefore I spoke, and we believe, therefore we speak. Therefore, the Spirit is one and the same, who is in the prophets and apostles, except that He was there for a moment, but here always. Moreover, there He was not always in them, but here He remains always in them, and there He was distributed in moderation, but here He was poured out entirely, there He was given sparingly, but here He was provided generously, and He was not exhibited before the resurrection of the Lord, but was given through the resurrection of Christ. For I will ask, He said, the Father, and He will give you another advocate, that He may be with you forever, the Spirit of truth. And: When the advocate comes, whom I will send to you from my Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from my Father. And: If I do not go away, the advocate will not come to you, but if I go away, I will send Him to you. And: When the Spirit of truth comes, He will guide you into all truth. And since the Lord was about to depart into heaven, He necessarily gave the paraclete to the disciples, lest He leave them as orphans, which was not fitting, and abandon them without an advocate and a guardian. For this is He who strengthened their minds and spirits, who distinguished the sacraments of the Gospel, who was the illuminator of divine things in them, by whom they were confirmed to confess the name of the Lord, and they did not fear prisons or chains, but rather trampled upon the powers of the world and its torments, armed and strengthened by Him, having in themselves the gifts that this same Spirit distributed and directed to the church of Christ, the bride, as if they were ornaments. This is He who established prophets in the church, taught masters, directed languages, worked virtues and healings, performed miraculous works, distributed discernments of spirits, contributed governances, suggested counsels, and composed and arranged the gifts of charisms, and thus made the church of the Lord perfect and complete in every way. This is He who, in the form of a dove, came upon the Lord after He was baptized and remained, dwelling in Christ alone, full and complete, not mutilated in any measure or part, but distributed and sent with all His abundance, so that others might receive a certain sharing of graces from Him, the fountain of the Holy Spirit remaining in Christ, so that from Him the streams of gifts and works might flow, the Holy Spirit dwelling abundantly in Christ. For the prophet Isaiah, prophesying, said: And the Spirit of wisdom and understanding will rest upon Him, the Spirit of counsel and strength, the Spirit of knowledge and piety, and He will fill Him with the Spirit of the fear of God. And in another place, in the person of the Lord Himself: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because He anointed me to preach the Gospel to the poor. Similarly, David: Therefore, God, your God, anointed you with the oil of joy, beyond your companions. The apostle Paul says: For whoever does not have the Spirit of Christ, he is not His. And: Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. This is He who works a second birth from water, a certain seed of divine generation, and the consecrator of heavenly birth, a pledge of the promised inheritance, and a kind of guarantee of eternal salvation, who makes us the temple of God and His house. Who intercedes for us with divine ears with inexpressible groans, filling the office of advocacy and exhibiting the gifts of defense, dwelling in our bodies, given to us, and effecting sanctity, who, doing this in us, produces our bodies for eternity and the resurrection of immortality, while He accustoms them to be mixed with heavenly virtue and associated with the divine eternity of the Holy Spirit. For our bodies are instructed in Him and through Him to progress towards immortality, while they learn to moderate themselves according to His decrees. This is He who desires against the flesh, because the flesh resists Him. This is He who restrains insatiable desires, breaks immoderate lusts, extinguishes illicit passions, conquers burning impulses, rejects drunkenness, repels avarice, flees luxurious feasts, binds charities, constrains affections, repels sects, expedites the rule of truth, conquers heretics, and spits out the wicked. The apostle says about this: For we have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God. He exults and says: I think that I too have the Spirit of God. He says: And the Spirit of prophets is subject to prophets. He reports: The Spirit explicitly says that in the last times some will depart from the faith, giving attention to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons, speaking lies in hypocrisy, and no one has ever said anathema to Jesus, no one has denied Christ, the Son of God, or repudiated the Creator God, no one has spoken words against the Scriptures, no one has established other and sacrilegious decrees, no one has written different laws. Whoever blasphemes against this Spirit will not have remission, not only in this age but also in the future. This Spirit testifies to Christ in the apostles, shows constant faith of religion in martyrs, includes admirable continence of sealed chastity in virgins, keeps the incorrupt and uncontaminated laws of the Lord's doctrine in others, destroys heretics, corrects the perverse, accuses the faithless, shows hypocrites, corrects the wicked, and keeps the church incorrupt and inviolable in perpetual virginity and the sanctity of truth.

pass_b_english: Reason's order and faith's authority, having set the Lord's words and letters in order, urge us to believe also in the Holy Spirit, who was promised to the church but given at the appointed times (Joel 2:28-29). He was promised through the prophet Joel, yet given through Christ. 'In the last days,' He says, 'I will pour out my Spirit upon my servants and handmaids' (Joel 2:28-29). The Lord Himself said, 'Receive the Holy Spirit; whose sins you forgive, they are forgiven, and whose sins you retain, they are retained' (John 20:22-23). The Lord Christ calls this Holy Spirit a paraclete and declares Him to be the Spirit of truth. He is not new in the Gospel, nor was He newly given. For this same Spirit accused the people in the prophets and provided advocacy to the nations in the apostles. The people deserved accusation because they despised the law, while those who believe from the nations deserve the Spirit's advocacy because they strive to attain the law of the Gospel. There is indeed a difference in the kinds of offices, since the reason for the causes differs at different times. Nevertheless, He who does these things is not different, nor is He another when He acts this way; He is one and the same, dividing His offices through times, occasions, and moments.

Finally, the apostle Paul says: 'Having the same Spirit, as it is written, "I believed, therefore I spoke," and we believe, therefore we speak.' Therefore, the Spirit is one and the same, who is in the prophets and apostles, except that He was there for a moment, but here He remains always. Moreover, there He was not always in them, but here He remains always in them; there He was distributed in moderation, but here He was poured out entirely; there He was given sparingly, but here He is provided generously. And He was not exhibited before the Lord's resurrection, but was given through Christ's resurrection. For He said, 'I will ask the Father, and He will give you another advocate, that He may be with you forever, the Spirit of truth' (John 14:16-17). And: 'When the advocate comes, whom I will send to you from my Father, the Spirit of truth, who proceeds from my Father' (John 15:26). And: 'If I do not go away, the advocate will not come to you; but if I go away, I will send Him to you' (John 16:7). And: 'When the Spirit of truth comes, He will guide you into all truth' (John 16:13). And since the Lord was about to depart into heaven, He necessarily gave the paraclete to the disciples, lest He leave them as orphans, which was not fitting, and abandon them without an advocate and a guardian.

For this is He who strengthened their minds and spirits, who distinguished the sacraments of the Gospel, who was the illuminator of divine things in them, by whom they were confirmed to confess the name of the Lord, and they did not fear prisons or chains; indeed, they trampled upon the powers of the world and its torments, armed and strengthened by Him, having in themselves the gifts that this same Spirit distributed and directed to the church of Christ, the bride, as if they were ornaments. This is He who established prophets in the church, taught masters, directed languages, worked virtues and healings, performed miraculous works, distributed discernments of spirits, contributed governances, suggested counsels, and composed and arranged the gifts of charisms, and thus made the church of the Lord perfect and complete in every way.

This is He who, in the form of a dove, came upon the Lord after He was baptized and remained, dwelling in Christ alone, full and complete, not mutilated in any measure or part, but distributed and sent with all His abundance, so that others might receive a certain sharing of graces from Him, the fountain of the Holy Spirit remaining in Christ, so that from Him the streams of gifts and works might flow, the Holy Spirit dwelling abundantly in Christ. For the prophet Isaiah, prophesying, said: 'And the Spirit of wisdom and understanding will rest upon Him, the Spirit of counsel and strength, the Spirit of knowledge and piety, and He will fill Him with the Spirit of the fear of God' (Isaiah 11:2-3). And in another place, in the person of the Lord Himself: 'The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because He anointed me to preach the Gospel to the poor' (Luke 4:18). Similarly, David: 'Therefore, God, your God, anointed you with the oil of joy, beyond your companions.' The apostle Paul says: 'For whoever does not have the Spirit of Christ, he is not His.' And: 'Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty' (2 Corinthians 3:17).

This is He who works a second birth from water, a certain seed of divine generation, and the consecrator of heavenly birth, a pledge of the promised inheritance, and a kind of guarantee of eternal salvation, who makes us the temple of God and His house. He intercedes for us with divine ears with inexpressible groans, filling the office of advocacy and exhibiting the gifts of defense, dwelling in our bodies, given to us, and effecting sanctity. Doing this in us, He produces our bodies for eternity and the resurrection of immortality, while He accustoms them to be mixed with heavenly virtue and associated with the divine eternity of the Holy Spirit. For our bodies are instructed in Him and through Him to progress towards immortality, while they learn to moderate themselves according to His decrees. This is He who desires against the flesh, because the flesh resists Him. This is He who restrains insatiable desires, breaks immoderate lusts, extinguishes illicit passions, conquers burning impulses, rejects drunkenness, repels avarice, flees luxurious feasts, binds charities, constrains affections, repels sects, expedites the rule of truth, conquers heretics, and spits out the wicked.

The apostle says about this: 'For we have not received the spirit of the world, but the Spirit who is from God.' He exults and says: 'I think that I too have the Spirit of God.' He says: 'And the Spirit of prophets is subject to prophets.' He reports: 'The Spirit explicitly says that in the last times some will depart from the faith, giving attention to seducing spirits and doctrines of demons, speaking lies in hypocrisy.' And no one has ever said anathema to Jesus in this Spirit; no one has denied Christ, the Son of God, or repudiated the Creator God; no one has spoken words against the Scriptures; no one has established other and sacrilegious decrees; no one has written different laws. Whoever blasphemes against this Spirit will not have remission, not only in this age but also in the future. This Spirit testifies to Christ in the apostles, shows constant faith of religion in martyrs, includes admirable continence of sealed chastity in virgins, keeps the incorrupt and uncontaminated laws of the Lord's doctrine in others, destroys heretics, corrects the perverse, accuses the faithless, shows hypocrites, corrects the wicked, and keeps the church incorrupt and inviolable in perpetual virginity and the sanctity of truth.
